test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Nov, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Through thick and thin

options.text: To pass through thick and thin air
To be supportive in both good and bad times
To possess both thick and thin clothes
To travel through thick and thin clouds

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. To be supportive in both good and bad times. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Through thick and thin"** means to remain supportive and loyal in all circumstances, whether they are good or bad. (सुख-दुख में साथ देना) • **Example:** She stood by her best friend through thick and thin, no matter what challenges they faced. • **"Thick and Thin"** refers to extremes or variations in conditions, emphasizing loyalty and support regardless of the situation. (बुरे और अच्छे समय) • **Example:** A true friend is someone who stays with you through thick and thin. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 1: To pass through thick and thin air** (मोटी और पतली हवा के बीच से गुजरना): This option is incorrect as it misinterprets the idiom. • **Example:** This phrase does not have a valid meaning in English. • **Option 3: To possess both thick and thin clothes** (मोटी और पतली कपड़े रखना): This option is unrelated to the idiom and refers to having different types of clothing. • **Example:** I packed both thick and thin clothes for my trip to the mountains. • **Option 4: To travel through thick and thin clouds** (मोटी और पतली बादलों के बीच से यात्रा करना): This option incorrectly assumes the idiom refers to physical travel. • **Example:** Pilots often navigate through thick and thin clouds during flights, but this has no connection to the idiom. ec:Tb88, The correct answer is: **Honorary**.
